content:
Hi, I’m Pragyan Manadhata, a high school student interested in number theory and Lean. I’m currently formalizing parts of Cox’s Primes of the Form x² + ny² and the proof of the Erdős primitive set conjecture.

The Cox project has produced a few results that may be useful for Mathlib, including a criterion for when −3 is a square modulo a prime, Jacobi-symbol periodicity, work on binary quadratic forms and Gauss reduction, and a Gaussian-integer norm lemma.

I’ve collected my drafts and notes here. Nothing has been submitted yet, but I wanted to introduce the project and share what I’ve been working on. I’d appreciate any general feedback.

Cox' book is great, and my instinct is to keep going with it and not to worry too much about upstreaming to mathlib right now. Figuring out when -3 is a square mod p is an easy consequence of quadratic reciprocity, for example, and it's not immediately clear to me that mathlib wants it. Similarly the result about prime Gaussian integers will be true in far more generality (and mathlib cares about getting things proved in the right generality) but as I say I would consider not worrying too much about mathlib now and instead considering how far through the book you can get.
